conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education and Board of County Commissioners Joint Quarterly Meeting |
conflicts.issue: Sizing the 2026 School Bond and Potential Small-School Consolidation Amid County Capital Constraints
conflicts.summary: While DPS presented ~$965M in immediate FCA needs (~$2B long-term) and highlighted 13 under-enrolled elementary schools (<450 students), county leadership emphasized severe county revenue constraints ($11M sales tax shortfall, county hiring freezes, and >$2B competing 10-year CIP requests) requiring tough trade-offs on bond sizing and school footprint consolidation.
conflicts.side_a_position: Address comprehensive district facility equity, deferred maintenance (~$965M FCA), and modernizations across all campuses through a major 2026 bond while carefully studying 5 consolidation trade-up candidates through the CIP Task Force.
side_a_arguments: Every DPS campus deserves modernized learning environments after years of deferred maintenance.
Community trust requires transparent objective CIP Task Force evaluation before closing or consolidating small neighborhood elementary schools.
conflicts.side_b_position: Align DPS capital requests strictly with Durham County debt capacity, sales tax revenue pressures, and realistic project phasing, while pursuing consolidation efficiencies where elementary schools remain under 450 students.
side_b_arguments: Durham County faces an $11M sales tax shortfall, federal safety-net pressures, and over $2B in countywide capital demands requiring strict debt limits.
Operating 13 elementary schools below 450 students creates ongoing capital and operating inefficiencies unless consolidation or co-location options are weighed.
conflicts.resolution: No formal bond vote was taken; both boards agreed to add an extra Q1 2026 joint budget session before May 12 to coordinate capital and operating requests early.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education and Board of County Commissioners Joint Quarterly Meeting |
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education and the Durham County Board of County Commissioners convened for their joint quarterly meeting (held Wednesday, November 19 and published November 20, 2025), co-chaired by BOE Chair Bettina Umstead and BOCC Chair Nida Allam. Both boards addressed recent immigration enforcement fears and school visitor protocols, reviewed DPS's $965 million Facility Condition Assessment and early 2026 school bond planning alongside County Manager Claudia Hager's sobering FY 2025-26 revenue update ($11 million sales tax shortfall and $2B+ 10-year county CIP), and examined DPS's state accountability gains (88.9% meeting/exceeding growth, ranking #1 among NC's 12 largest districts). The joint bodies approved the agenda, the August 12 joint meeting minutes, and an amended 2026 joint calendar adding a Q1 budget meeting before May 12, followed by public comment advocating affordable housing on a 3-acre parcel at the current Durham School of the Arts site.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks on Immigration Enforcement, Agenda Approval, and August 12 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: BOE Chair Bettina Umstead and BOCC Chair Nida Allam opened the joint quarterly meeting with remarks addressing heightened Customs and Border Protection / ICE activity in Durham and emphasizing visitor protocols keeping students safe. The joint boards unanimously approved the meeting agenda and the August 12, 2025 joint meeting minutes.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Agenda approved unanimously; August 12 minutes approved unanimously

agenda_items.title: DPS Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Process and 2026 Bond Outlook
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS leadership and planning staff presented findings from the district's $965 million Facility Condition Assessment—translating to roughly $2 billion in total long-term facility needs—alongside work by the CIP Task Force on 13 elementary schools enrolling under 450 students and 5 potential consolidation trade-up candidates. Commissioners and school board members questioned facility capacity, underutilized school footprints, and timing ahead of a targeted 2026 bond referendum.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Operating Budget and 10-Year CIP Fiscal Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Manager Claudia Hager outlined tight county fiscal conditions, reporting an $11 million FY 2024-25 sales tax shortfall, a $5.9 million per month SNAP gap, county hiring freezes, and more than $2 billion in competing 10-year county capital needs. Hager stressed early coordination between DPS and county finance staff before finalizing the 2026 bond sizing and operating expansion requests.

agenda_items.title: DPS 2024-25 Academic Accountability Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Al Royster and Dr. King presented 2024-25 academic results showing 56.6% of DPS schools earned A, B, or C grades, low-performing schools dropped from 20 to 17, overall GLP reached 48.4%, and 88.9% of schools met or exceeded growth—#1 among NC's 12 largest districts and well ahead of Durham charter schools (71.4%). BOCC Vice Chair Dr. Mike Lee criticized the state's 80% achievement / 20% growth school performance grade formula for penalizing high-growth schools.

agenda_items.title: 2026 Joint Quarterly Meeting Calendar
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Joint board members reviewed proposed 2026 quarterly meeting dates and agreed to add an extra Q1 joint BOCC-BOE budget meeting prior to May 12 to align county and school board budget cycles alongside joint City/County/DPS sessions.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment on Durham School of the Arts North Parcel Reuse
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Jim Svara urged the Board of Education and County Commissioners to explore developing affordable housing on a 3-acre north lot on the existing Durham School of the Arts campus adjacent to the Rail Trail once DSA relocates.

votes.notes: Joint BOCC-BOE voice vote; BOCC Chair Nida Allam seconded BOE Vice Chair Millicent Rogers's motion.
votes.discussion_detail: Following joint opening remarks from BOE Chair Bettina Umstead and BOCC Chair Nida Allam regarding community immigration concerns and school safety protocols, BOE Vice Chair Millicent Rogers moved to approve the joint quarterly meeting agenda as presented. BOCC Chair Nida Allam seconded the motion. No joint board members requested modifications, and the motion carried unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve August 12, 2025 Joint Quarterly Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Joint BOCC-BOE voice vote; BOCC Vice Chair Dr. Mike Lee moved and BOE member Natalie Beyer seconded.
votes.discussion_detail: BOCC Vice Chair Dr. Mike Lee moved to adopt the minutes of the August 12, 2025 joint quarterly meeting between the Board of Education and Board of County Commissioners, and BOE member Natalie Beyer seconded. No edits or corrections were raised by members of either board. The joint bodies approved the minutes unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve 2026 Joint Meeting Calendar as Amended to Add Q1 Budget Meeting Before May 12
votes.notes: Joint BOCC-BOE voice vote ensuring early joint budget coordination before May 12.
votes.discussion_detail: When reviewing the proposed 2026 joint quarterly meeting schedule, BOCC and BOE members agreed on the need to meet jointly earlier in the spring budget cycle rather than waiting until May 12. BOCC Vice Chair Dr. Mike Lee moved—with BOCC Chair Nida Allam seconding—to approve the 2026 joint calendar as amended to add a Q1 BOCC-BOE budget meeting before May 12 alongside planned City/County/DPS joint sessions. Both boards approved the amended schedule unanimously by voice vote.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education and Board of County Commissioners Joint Quarterly Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 13, 2025 joint quarterly meeting hosted by the Durham Public Schools (DPS) Board of Education with the Durham Board of County Commissioners, the joint boards unanimously approved the meeting agenda (moved by Wendy Jacobs, seconded by Natalie Beyer) and the February 18, 2025 meeting minutes (moved by Natalie Beyer, seconded by Joy Harrell-Goff) by voice vote, with no split or contested votes occurring. Staff (Ms. Mitchell) presented a preview of the district's Facility Conditions Assessment (FCA) and 5-to-10-year Capital Improvement Plan (CIP), highlighting newly completed middle and high school learning environment guidelines and reporting a $200 million-plus funding deficit on 2022 bond projects whose estimated costs rose from $423.5 million to $624 million. Later in the session, Commissioner Wendy Jacobs stressed finalizing written agreements prior to budget adoption, and Dr. Pittman announced that a Memorandum of Agreement (effective May 9, 2025) and a data-sharing agreement with Linda Chappelle's office had been executed. During public comment, Javana Lewis of Empower Parents and Community and the Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People urged both boards to center Black students and Exceptional Children in the budget and to fund $6.1 million in community-informed superintendent priorities.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Joint Board of County Commissioners and Board of Education quarterly meeting was called to order and opened with a review of the agenda. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs moved to approve the agenda and Board Member Natalie Beyer seconded the motion, which carried unanimously without discussion.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes from February 18, 2025
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The joint boards reviewed the minutes from the February 18, 2025 joint meeting. Board Member Natalie Beyer moved to approve the minutes and Board Member Joy Harrell-Goff seconded, passing unanimously by voice vote with no discussion.

agenda_items.title: Facility Conditions Assessment and Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Preview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ms. Mitchell presented an overview of DPS's long-range facility planning tools—the Facilities Master Plan, Facility Conditions Assessment (FCA), and 5-to-10-year Capital Improvement Plan (CIP)—alongside newly completed middle and high school learning environment guidelines. She compared the 2016 and 2022 bond funding models and reported that 2022 bond project costs have escalated from the allocated $423.5 million to $624 million, creating an unfunded deficit of just over $200 million. Staff proposed re-evaluating unaddressed 2022 bond components and accounting for three years of enrollment and facility changes ahead of the next 10-year cycle.

agenda_items.title: MOA and Data-Sharing Agreement Update Ahead of Budget Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the middle portion of the meeting, Commissioner Wendy Jacobs emphasized the importance of securing written documentation prior to adopting the annual budget. Dr. Pittman announced that a Memorandum of Agreement (effective Friday, May 9, 2025) and a data-sharing agreement developed with Linda Chappelle's office had been executed so the boards are ready for the year's data.

agenda_items.title: Public Comments and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Javana Lewis, representing Empower Parents and Community (EPIC) and the Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People (DCABP), cited over 130 petition signatures and urged both boards to prioritize academic growth for Black students, Exceptional Children supports, mental health and social-emotional learning, and teacher working conditions. She highlighted $6.1 million in the superintendent's proposed budget tied to community conversations and noted gaps between DPS requests and County Manager recommendations before the meeting adjourned at 03:05:34.

votes.discussion_detail: No discussion occurred prior to the voice vote.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners on 2025-02-18 9:00 AM - Joint BOCC/Board of Education Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: During the captured portion of the February 18, 2025 Joint BOCC and DPS Board of Education meeting (presided over by BOCC Chair Dr. Mike Lee), members focused on school transportation staffing, public transit access for students, pedestrian infrastructure, and constrained FY2025-26 budget prospects. Staff and board members reviewed the $417 CDL and DOT onboarding cost breakdown for bus drivers, bus-tracking app evaluations, biweekly driver pay, and the need to prioritize bus driver and monitor retention despite tight local budgets. Officials also examined sidewalk gaps around 15 secondary schools with public transit guides, Unified Development Ordinance/UDL streetscape standards, and cross-jurisdictional City-County-DPS coordination under the Safe Routes to School working group and joint Bike/Walk Plan. The County Manager warned that position freezes and fiscal tightening since November signal one of the toughest budget cycles nationwide, and the meeting adjourned cleanly on a unanimous voice vote with no contested or split votes recorded.

agenda_items.title: Bus Driver CDL Costs, Route Coverage, and Secondary School Transit Guides
agenda_items.discussion_summary: District staff discussed potential partnerships with NCCU for student bus drivers and detailed the $417 onboarding cost per driver ($80 CDL learner's permit, $106.50 CDL, up to $150 DOT physical, and $75-$80 DOT drug test), while Dr. Webb confirmed all routes were covered and committed to sharing on-time arrival and departure data. Ms. Brookshire reported that public transit guides had been distributed to 15 secondary schools (excluding outlying schools), though members noted uneven sidewalk access to bus stops and recommended distributing guides directly to families via school newsletters, robocalls, and shared folders.

agenda_items.title: Bus Safety App, Driver Pay, and Transportation Staffing Crisis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board Member Wendell Tabb asked about ongoing evaluations of the district's bus-tracking app and how parents are notified if a student misses or does not board a bus, with Dr. Webb explaining that absence alerts come from school attendance while school transportation coordinators track ridership and staff explore direct tracking options. Members thanked BOCC Chair Dr. Mike Lee for holding a CDL, confirmed bus drivers are paid every two weeks, and underscored the post-pandemic bus driver staffing crisis as a top budget priority for drivers and monitors.

agenda_items.title: UDL Streetscape Standards and City-County Safe Routes to School Coordination
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ms. Brookshire clarified how Unified Development Ordinance/UDL standards govern streetscapes and sidewalk widths for new and redeveloping areas, noting DPS had not submitted specific UDL proposals. In response to questions about students crossing between city and county jurisdictions, staff highlighted monthly and quarterly Safe Routes to School working group meetings (involving City Transportation, DPS, County Public Health and Transportation, Bike Durham, and NCDOT) and Durham's first joint City-County Bike/Walk Plan.

agenda_items.title: County Budget Outlook and High School Transit Ridership Initiative
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Responding to Board Member Natalie Beyer's request for budget framing ahead of the upcoming public forum and Friday retreat, the County Manager stated that position freezes and fiscal containment since November reflect one of the most challenging budget cycles nationwide. Members also echoed Councilmember Caballero's proposal from the joint City-County-Schools meeting to encourage high school students to use GoTriangle and City of Durham transit to support both public transit goals and DPS transportation capacity.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment Period and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee opened the public comment period, noting that the Clerk had one person signed up to speak, though no audience speaker came forward. Following a motion by Board Member Natalie Beyer and a second by a County Commissioner, the joint boards adjourned by unanimous voice vote.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Unanimous voice vote; bare adjournment skipped in votes)
